title: The front page shows the last backup
body:
## Summary The front page now ends with one quiet line saying when the last backup succeeded, "Last backup 5 hours ago", with the exact UTC time in the element's `title`. It turns amber, led by the 6px status dot, when the last success is more than 26 hours old, the latest attempt failed, nothing has succeeded yet, or the status file cannot be read. On the laptop, in CI and on the runner's stack `CORE_BACKUP_STATUS_FILE` is unset, so nothing is read and there is no line. Best read in this order: 1. `Core/src/backup_status.rs`, a new concept in the core. `setting` turns the value of `CORE_BACKUP_STATUS_FILE` into a path; unset gives none and a relative path is refused. `state(content, now)` is the pure function from the file's bytes and now to `Fine`, `Stale`, `Failed`, `NoSuccessYet` or `Unreadable`. `read` reads at most 4 KiB of a regular file. `BackupStatus::line` gives the words and the time to render. 2. `Core/src/relative.rs`: the rounding review's card already used for "in 3 hours", moved out of `cards.rs`, now with `ago` for "5 hours ago" as well. 3. `Core/src/lib.rs`: the setting is read at startup, before the database, and kept in `AppState.backup_status_file`. The front page handler reads the file on every load when it is set. 4. `Core/templates/front.html` and `Core/assets/core.css`: the `

` after the cards, plus `attention` with its `::before` dot. Tokens only. 5. `infra/hosted/compose.yaml`: the core mounts `backup_status` read only at `/status` and gets the setting. 6. `infra/hosted/check.sh` and `e2e/`: one `backup now` before the suite, the `backup_status` fixture, and the three e2e tests. 7. Docs. Closes #258 ## Tasks - [x] Add `CORE_BACKUP_STATUS_FILE` and the reading of the file into a state, with the unit tests: 16d58ec - [x] Add the line to the front page and its style, with the template tests: d997fd7 - [x] Mount the status volume into the core in `infra/hosted/compose.yaml`, and add the e2e tests and the screenshots: 74bedbd Docs: 456b34f. ## Decisions the agent made - **The relative time function is shared, not added beside the old one.** #238 left a private `relative` in `cards.rs` that only writes times ahead ("in 3 hours"). Settled says to use such a function if #238 added one, and otherwise to add one taking now. I moved its rounding into `src/relative.rs` with `ahead` and `ago`, and review's card now calls `relative::ahead`. Its existing test, `cards::tests::the_next_due_is_relative_to_now`, still passes unchanged. Alternative: a second copy of the rounding for times past. Why: one rule for how the platform says a time, kept in one place. - **Restoring the real file needs a read command too: `E2E_BACKUP_STATUS_READ`.** Settled gives `E2E_BACKUP_STATUS_WRITE` and says the fixture restores the real file afterwards, which means reading it first. `check.sh` sets `E2E_BACKUP_STATUS_READ` to ` backup cat /status/backup.json`, the same `docker compose exec` into the backup container, and the fixture fails naming whichever variable is missing. Alternative: restore by writing a freshly made "success now" file, which is not the real file and would hide what the backup job last wrote. Why: it matches Settled's restore and follows the pattern of `E2E_CORE_COMMAND`. No helper goes into the image. - **A failed latest attempt outranks staleness.** When the last attempt failed and the last success is also older than 26 hours, the line says "the latest attempt failed" rather than "none since". Alternative: stale first. Why: the failure is the more specific news and points at the log. The unit test `a_failed_last_attempt_needs_attention_even_after_a_recent_success` covers both ages. - **A success more than five minutes ahead of now is `Unreadable`.** Within five minutes it is fine, shown as "just now". Alternative: accept any future time as fine. Why: a future `last_success_at` would read as fine forever and hide a stopped backup; on correctness, the stricter option. Test: `a_success_ahead_of_now_is_fine_only_within_the_skew`. - **Every field is required, `last_error` included, and a success with no time is "No backup has succeeded yet".** Plain serde reads an absent `Option` as null, so `last_error` goes through a deserializer that makes it required, as `ReviewCard.next_due_at` does. Only a JSON object reads, as with the cards. `last_attempt_ok: true` with `last_success_at: null` has no success to show, so it gets the "no success yet" words. Why: "a type that refuses unknown fields, as the cards do" in Settled, applied to missing fields as well. - **Only a regular file is read.** `read` checks the metadata before opening, so a directory or a pipe at the path is `Unreadable` rather than read or waited on. Tokio's `fs` and `io-util` features are turned on for this. No new crate, and `Cargo.lock` is unchanged. - **The dot is a CSS `::before`, the time a `` element.** The dot is decoration; the words carry the state, so the rule "a dot plus a word, never colour alone" holds for a screen reader too. `` carries the exact time both machine readable and on hover. The time is in the mono font, following rule 8 of `design/DESIGN.md` and the slice's Context. In the screenshots that leaves wide word gaps in "2 days ago", since a monospace space is a full cell. It is legible, but worth a glance. - **The settings test runs the real binary.** `tests/settings.rs` starts `platform_core` from an empty directory, so no `.env` is loaded, with every setting read before the database. A relative path must exit naming `CORE_BACKUP_STATUS_FILE` before the database is asked for; unset and absolute must get as far as asking for `CORE_APP_DATABASE_URL`. - **The docs' reason for "a file, not a call or a table" is mine.** Settled asked the doc to say why, but the feature issue does not record a reason. What I wrote: the job is a script on a schedule and does not listen; a table would give the read only backup role a write grant and put the record of backups inside what is backed up; a file says the truth even when Postgres is down. ## Verification Gate, for the areas `changed-areas.sh` printed as true (`core=true canary=false brain=false libs=false scripts=false web=false e2e=true dotnet_services=[]`), at 456b34f: - core, from `Core/`: `cargo fmt --check` ok; `bash scripts/agent/services.sh run core migrate`: "nothing to do, every migration is applied"; `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --locked`: 198 passed, 0 failed (summed over every test binary); `cargo test --locked --test app_roles -- --ignored`: 3 passed; `cargo sqlx prepare --check -- --all-targets --locked` ok. - e2e, against the dev stack started from the branch (frontends built, Caddy recreated, every service healthy): `UV_LOCKED=1 uv run playwright install chromium` ok; `UV_LOCKED=1 uv run pytest`: 275 passed, 4 deselected (the two `hosted_only` tests at two viewports); `ruff check`: all checks passed; `ruff format --check`: 24 files already formatted. - Hosted, not part of CI: `bash infra/hosted/check.sh` exited 0 with `9 passed, 0 failed`. Its suite ran 278 passed, 1 deselected (the `dev_stack_only` test), the hosted backup tests included, and `backup_test` passed 12 of 12. `infra/hosted/tests/agree.test.sh`: 32 passed. - Volume ownership, checked by hand: a fresh volume mounted first read only by the core's image, then by the backup image, is owned by the backup user (uid 10001) and writable by it. Docker copies the image's ownership onto a volume that is still empty, and the core never writes there, so start order does not matter. Acceptance tests, failing before the change, against stubs returning a wrong state: ``` $ cargo test --locked --lib -- backup_status test backup_status::tests::a_recent_success_reads_as_fine ... FAILED test backup_status::tests::a_success_older_than_26_hours_is_stale ... FAILED test backup_status::tests::a_failed_last_attempt_needs_attention_even_after_a_recent_success ... FAILED test backup_status::tests::no_success_yet_needs_attention ... FAILED test backup_status::tests::a_missing_unreadable_or_malformed_file_needs_attention ... FAILED test backup_status::tests::without_the_setting_there_is_no_status ... FAILED left: Unreadable right: Fine { last_success: 2027-01-15 3:00:00.0 +00:00:00 } left: Ok(None) right: Ok(Some("/status/backup.json")) test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 8 failed $ cargo test --locked --test settings test a_backup_status_path_that_is_not_absolute_refuses_startup ... FAILED "backup.json": Error: "CORE_APP_DATABASE_URL: environment variable not found" $ cargo test --locked --test front_page test the_backup_line_renders_each_state ... FAILED fine:

Last backup 5 hours ago

missing from test result: FAILED. 6 passed; 1 failed ``` and passing after it: ``` $ cargo test --locked --lib -- backup_status relative cards test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed $ cargo test --locked --test settings test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed $ cargo test --locked --test front_page test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed $ bash infra/hosted/check.sh tests/test_front_page.py .......... ok the_acceptance_suite_passes_against_the_containers 9 passed, 0 failed ``` Screenshots, desktop and 390px phone width: The backup line, from the hosted run in `check.sh` (fine, then tests.** I wrote the two `hosted_only` tests after the core change, and the dev suite cannot run them; they ran only in the green `check.sh` run. The dev test `test_the_home_page_says_nothing_about_backups_without_the_setting` checks for an absence, so it passes on `main` as well. To see them fail, run `check.sh` with the core's `CORE_BACKUP_STATUS_FILE` line removed from `infra/hosted/compose.yaml`. - **CI does not run `check.sh`**, as `infra/hosted/README.md` says, so the hosted tests and their screenshots come from my local run only. ## Doc changes - `Core/docs/core-architecture.md`: new section, "The backup line on the front page", as Settled asked. It covers what the line reads, the 26 hour and skew rules, that it is an operator's signal shown to every account for now, and why it is a file. - `infra/hosted/README.md`: "Backups" says where the result shows, replacing "Nothing alerts on a missed backup yet" with the line plus that sentence. The `the_acceptance_suite_passes_against_the_containers` case now mentions `backup now` and the two status variables. - `e2e/README.md`: the `backup_status` fixture; "Markers", where "No test carries it today" for `dev_stack_only` is no longer true; and the command block under "Against the hosted copy". - `docs/README.md`: the index line for `core-architecture.md` lists the new section. - `Core/.env.example`: the setting, commented out, with one line.
